title: The case list is served twice in the target, and the row names, the bounds, the login and the flag mechanism of the owner's list have no source
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-033 sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 15; Recovery Workbench FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.19 and A2.38; Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 (case list, queue_measure); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8 and 10; _work/msr/context/P3.md ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R5.5, R7.2 and R9
section: s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 Business rules BR2 and BR7; s10 Authority; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Solution plan; s14 Validation and messages; s15 Screens and states; s18 Traceability
description: Seven items of this slice have no value or no single value in the sources. (a) The legacy list is composed on the integration base by RWB-P2-E2033-APP and served on the owner's base by this story, so the same page exists twice in the target and no source says which one the SCR-02 route reads. (b) The legacy story names the response fields ageDays, serviceLevelDueAt, serviceLevelState and prescriptionClockStatus but not the envelope, the filter token list, the row element names or the problem body, and RWB-P2-E2033-CON does not fix them for this base. (c) The page-size bounds are not stated as parameter rows anywhere, and the legacy story only fixes the range 1 to 200 in its flow and exception rows. (d) Legacy BR2 defines age in state from stage_clock_start and returns it as ageDays, while RWB-P3-E2011-APP publishes ageDays as the age from the entry date, so one field name carries two meanings. (e) The legacy index ix_timer_case_type on timer (case_id, timer_type) is already landed by RWB-P3-E2011-APP as ix_timer_case_type_status on three columns, and no source says whether the legacy index is still wanted. (f) The rwb-case database login name, the owner of the switch rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing and the switch mechanism are not stated. (g) The platform unavailable message MSG-GEN-006 has no text in any source, and REQ-ACA-006 still names a data-lake copy that DP-17 removes.
evidence: RWB-E2-033 section 12 (GET /api/recovery/v1/cases response fields), section 8 BR2 and BR7, section 13 (CREATE INDEX ix_timer_case_type on timer), section 4 step 2 (GET /api/recovery/v1/cases), section 14 (MSG-GEN-006 with no text); FSD P3 v4 A2.19 AC-P3-019-01 and AC-EXC-P3-019-02 (export limit 10000); context pack P3 REST rows (22 operations) and tables (timer); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 row, DP-06 row, DP-07 row, DP-14 row, DP-15 row and DP-17 row; Architecture v5 slide 8 (19 rwb_* schemas, one login each).
proposed: At the RWB-P2-E2033-CON baseline review, state that the composed SCR-02 page reads rwb-integration and the owner base serves the same rows to it, fix the row and envelope names in version 1 of the contract, confirm the page bounds and the export limit as parameter rows with RWB-P3-E2011-APP, keep ageDays as the age since entry with ageInStateDays added, drop the duplicate timer index, and name the login and the flag owner in the rwb-case baseline.
